Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature

All polyamides take up water when kept in a moist environment. At room temperature this is a physical process which is reversible. Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis. Water uptake is mainly dependent on the amide group concentration of the individual polyamide type. For this reason, polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.
They resist fuels, lubricants and most chemicals, but are attacked by phenols, strong acids and oxidizing agents.

Boiling water (stagnant) and 80 °C aerated water tests; service life depends on temperature and oxygen content

Zytel nylon resins are resistant to hot water and steam. Thus, Zytel has found wide uses in such applications as hot water mixing valves, gears and baskets, equipment used for conveying in hot water and parts which must be subjected to steam, as in a sterilization cycle. Factors important to performance: a 15 °C increase in temperature may reduce life by 40-50 %; service life is shorter in oxygen-rich water.
p. 39, 5.3 Resistance of Zytel to hot water and steam

Natural and pigmented Zytel nylon resins have only moderate resistance to the effects of sunlight but special weather-resistant compositions retain their properties and appearance for years. Table 5.05 Florida weathering: Zytel 101 NC010 (66 nylon, not stabilized) tensile strength 73 MPa initially, 37 MPa after 6 months, elongation 300 % to 10 %; Zytel 105 BK010A (light stabilized, black) 63 to 62 MPa and 160 % to 60 %.
Water absorption at 50 % RH and 100 % RH

Nylons absorb moisture from the air and 66 nylon equilibrates at about 2,8 % water at 50 % RH and at about 8,5 % at 100 % RH. This plasticizes the nylon, lowering its strength and stiffness but increasing its toughness and elongation. Moisture absorption increases dimensions of 66 nylons by 0,6 % at 50 % RH and about 2,6 % at 100 % RH.
